reuse.why: applyWeekendRule and isNonWorkingDay are shared and used by the move path everywhere, but the daily-skip and look-ahead logic is rewritten at each consumer instead of being part of the shared definition.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && frequency === daily => filter out non-working days' rule is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange) with three different look-ahead bounds, plus a fourth variant of the condition in schedule-template.

placement.why: The move rule and holiday check sit correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip variation lives in server/schedules/app.ts and the budget template rather than in the shared rule.

scope.why: Changes follow the requested steps; minor noise such as `movesWeekends ? true : false` and a duplicated word in a comment.

maintainability.why: The Step 0 goal of one definition erodes: each later step adds its own daily/holiday handling at call sites, so a future change to the weekend rule still has to be made in several places with divergent padding heuristics.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange handle daily schedules with their own isNonWorkingDay filter outside applyWeekendRule; budget/schedule-template.ts computes its own movesWeekends gate around applyWeekendRule

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip filter appears reshaped as a find() over take 7+holidays in getNextDate, a filter().slice() over count*4+holidays in getUpcomingDates, and a Set loop with padding 3+holidays in getDatesInRange

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend/applyWeekendRule gain skipWeekend and holidays parameters; shared getNextDate gains a daily special-case branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template decide the daily case themselves outside the shared rule
